data.name: DataTypes_Title
data.value: Data types and dynamic typing

data.name: DataTypes_Summary
data.value: SQLite checks types less strictly than MSSQL. A column has only a type affinity, and the stored value keeps its own type.

data.name: DataTypes_Point1
data.value: Type names such as INT, NVARCHAR(50) or DATETIME are accepted but only evaluated as an affinity (text, integer, floating point or numeric).

data.name: DataTypes_Point2
data.value: The length in VARCHAR(n) is not enforced. Texts that are too long are stored, while MSSQL rejects them with error 8152.

data.name: DataTypes_Point3
data.value: A value that cannot be converted to the column type is stored anyway. MSSQL reports error 245 in this case.

data.name: DataTypes_Point4
data.value: INT and BIGINT are always 64 bits wide in SQLite. The overflow at 2147483647 (error 8115) does not occur in calculations or when storing values. CAST and CONVERT check the range like MSSQL, though.

data.name: DataTypes_Point5
data.value: CAST and CONVERT to INT, SMALLINT, TINYINT, BIGINT, DECIMAL, FLOAT and BIT convert strictly. Text that cannot be converted causes error 245 (or 8114 for DECIMAL and FLOAT), and a value that is too large causes error 8115 or 248. CAST('1.5' AS INT) fails as in MSSQL, while CAST(1.5 AS INT) returns 1.

data.name: DataTypes_Point6
data.value: CAST and CONVERT to CHAR(n) and NCHAR(n) pad with spaces to length n, while VARCHAR(n) and NVARCHAR(n) truncate. Without a length, CAST and CONVERT use length 30.

data.name: DataTypes_Point7
data.value: BIT is a number (0 or 1). A text value such as 'true' is not converted in comparisons, but CAST('true' AS BIT) works.

data.name: Numbers_Title
data.value: Numbers, decimals and division

data.name: Numbers_Summary
data.value: DECIMAL, NUMERIC and MONEY are ordinary numbers in SQLite, so calculations and output differ in some details.

data.name: Numbers_Point1
data.value: Decimal values are stored as integers or floating-point numbers. Calculations are not exact as in MSSQL.

data.name: Numbers_Point2
data.value: The output has no fixed number of decimal places. MSSQL shows 5.00 for DECIMAL(10,2), while this environment shows 5 or 5.0.

data.name: Numbers_Point3
data.value: CAST(x AS DECIMAL(p, s)) rounds to s decimal places, but the result remains a floating-point number.

data.name: Numbers_Point4
data.value: Integer divided by integer returns an integer as in MSSQL (7 / 2 is 3). With a decimal operand the result is fractional (7 / 2.0 is 3.5, MSSQL shows 3.500000).

data.name: Numbers_Point5
data.value: Division and modulo by 0 raise error 8134 (Divide by zero error) as in MSSQL, including with decimals. A NULL divisor returns NULL.

data.name: Numbers_Point6
data.value: The % operator also works with decimals as in MSSQL (7.5 % 2 is 1.5).

data.name: Numbers_Point7
data.value: AVG over an integer column returns an integer in MSSQL (the average of 1 and 2 is 1) but a decimal in this environment (1.5).

data.name: Numbers_Point8
data.value: ROUND, CEILING, FLOOR, POWER, SQRT, SQUARE, SIGN, LOG, LOG10, EXP and PI are available as in MSSQL. ROUND also accepts negative lengths and the third parameter for truncating.

data.name: DatesAndTimes_Title
data.value: Date and time

data.name: DatesAndTimes_Summary
data.value: SQLite has no date types. This environment stores dates as ISO text and reproduces the most important MSSQL functions.

data.name: DatesAndTimes_Point1
data.value: DATE, DATETIME and DATETIME2 are stored as ISO text, for example 2024-03-01 or 2024-03-01 10:00:00.000. Comparisons and sorting work as long as all values use this format.

data.name: DatesAndTimes_Point2
data.value: GETDATE, GETUTCDATE, SYSDATETIME, SYSUTCDATETIME, DATEADD, DATEDIFF, DATEPART, DATENAME, YEAR, MONTH, DAY, EOMONTH, DATEFROMPARTS and ISDATE are reproduced.

data.name: DatesAndTimes_Point3
data.value: DATEDIFF counts crossed boundaries as in MSSQL, not complete intervals. DATEDIFF(year, '2023-12-31', '2024-01-01') is 1.

data.name: DatesAndTimes_Point4
data.value: Week numbering follows the MSSQL default with weeks starting on Sunday (DATEFIRST 7). DATENAME returns English month and weekday names.

data.name: DatesAndTimes_Point5
data.value: A value without a time stays a date after DATEADD. MSSQL always returns DATETIME with a time for a text literal.

data.name: DatesAndTimes_Point6
data.value: Date plus or minus a number (for example OrderDate + 7) is only converted when the date type is recognized, for example for a column of type DATE or for GETDATE().

data.name: DatesAndTimes_Point7
data.value: CAST(date AS VARCHAR) returns the stored ISO text. For other formats, use CONVERT(VARCHAR, value, style) with the styles 0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 8, 11, 12, 20, 21, 23, 100, 101, 103, 104, 105, 108, 111, 112, 120, 121 and 126, or use FORMAT.

data.name: DatesAndTimes_Point8
data.value: GETDATE returns the local time of the device if the runtime knows the time zone, and UTC otherwise.

data.name: DatesAndTimes_Point9
data.value: DATETRUNC, AT TIME ZONE, DATETIMEOFFSET and SWITCHOFFSET are not available.

data.name: Collation_Title
data.value: Case sensitivity, collation and trailing spaces

data.name: Collation_Summary
data.value: MSSQL compares text case-insensitively by default. SQLite compares it in binary.

data.name: Collation_Point1
data.value: The text columns of the tables in this environment are created with COLLATE NOCASE. Comparisons, sorting and GROUP BY on these columns therefore behave as in MSSQL.

data.name: Collation_Point2
data.value: String literals and computed expressions do not have this collation. 'a' = 'A' is false in this environment and true in MSSQL.

data.name: Collation_Point3
data.value: In SQLite, LIKE ignores case only for ASCII letters. For umlauts it is case-sensitive: 'Ä' LIKE 'ä' is false. UPPER and LOWER also handle umlauts in this environment.

data.name: Collation_Point4
data.value: MSSQL ignores trailing spaces in comparisons ('a' = 'a ' is true), SQLite does not. LEN ignores them like MSSQL.

data.name: Collation_Point5
data.value: CHARINDEX and REPLACE ignore case like MSSQL with the default collation.

data.name: Collation_Point6
data.value: LIKE supports only the wildcards % and _. Character classes such as [a-c] are not available.

data.name: Collation_Point7
data.value: COLLATE with SQL Server collations such as Latin1_General_CI_AS is not available. Use COLLATE NOCASE or COLLATE BINARY.

data.name: NullBehavior_Title
data.value: NULL and sorting

data.name: NullBehavior_Summary
data.value: MSSQL and this environment agree on the most important points of NULL handling.

data.name: NullBehavior_Point1
data.value: NULL sorts as the lowest value: it comes first with ASC and last with DESC. This matches MSSQL.

data.name: NullBehavior_Point2
data.value: Concatenation with NULL returns NULL ('a' + NULL is NULL), as in the MSSQL default.

data.name: NullBehavior_Point3
data.value: An empty string ('') is not NULL.

data.name: NullBehavior_Point4
data.value: Aggregate functions ignore NULL as in MSSQL. The warning 'Null value is eliminated by an aggregate' does not appear.

data.name: RowLimiting_Title
data.value: Limiting rows and paging

data.name: RowLimiting_Summary
data.value: TOP and OFFSET ... FETCH are translated to LIMIT and OFFSET.

data.name: RowLimiting_Point1
data.value: TOP n, TOP (n) and TOP (@variable) are placed as LIMIT after the respective query, including in subqueries, CTEs and parts of a UNION.

data.name: RowLimiting_Point2
data.value: OFFSET n ROWS FETCH NEXT m ROWS ONLY becomes LIMIT m OFFSET n. Without FETCH, all remaining rows are returned.

data.name: RowLimiting_Point3
data.value: TOP n PERCENT and TOP n WITH TIES are not available yet. Use ROW_NUMBER or RANK instead.

data.name: RowLimiting_Point4
data.value: TOP in INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE is not available yet.

data.name: RowLimiting_Point5
data.value: Without ORDER BY, the order of the rows is not defined, as in MSSQL.

data.name: RowLimiting_Point6
data.value: INTERSECT binds more tightly than UNION and EXCEPT, as in MSSQL.

data.name: Strings_Title
data.value: Strings

data.name: Strings_Summary
data.value: The + operator is translated to addition or concatenation based on the detected types.

data.name: Strings_Point1
data.value: The + operator becomes the SQLite concatenation || if one operand is detected as text and the other is not a numeric type. The types come from literals, CAST, functions and the columns of the tables.

data.name: Strings_Point2
data.value: Number + number stays an addition. '1' + 1 returns the number 2 as in MSSQL, and '2' + '3' returns the text 23.

data.name: Strings_Point3
data.value: For an expression of unknown type without a text operand, + stays an addition.

data.name: Strings_Point4
data.value: The prefix N in N'text' is removed. All texts are Unicode.

data.name: Strings_Point5
data.value: ISNULL returns the type of the first argument as in MSSQL. A replacement value of another type is converted accordingly.

data.name: Strings_Point6
data.value: STRING_AGG with WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ...) is available.

data.name: Strings_Point7
data.value: FORMAT uses .NET format strings as MSSQL does. Without a culture, en-US applies, and an empty culture means the invariant culture.

data.name: Strings_Point8
data.value: FORMAT knows the cultures en-US, en-GB, de-DE, fr-FR, es-ES and it-IT and the short forms en, de, fr, es and it. Any other culture raises error 9818 (The culture parameter is not supported), even if MSSQL knows it.

data.name: VariablesAndBatches_Title
data.value: Variables, batches and GO

data.name: VariablesAndBatches_Summary
data.value: GO is not a T-SQL command but a separator of the editor. Variables are valid only within their batch.

data.name: VariablesAndBatches_Point1
data.value: GO must be alone on a line, optionally with a repeat count (GO 3). GO is not recognized as a separator in strings and comments.

data.name: VariablesAndBatches_Point2
data.value: DECLARE, SET, SET with += and the use of @variables are available. After GO, all variables are unknown again (error 137).

data.name: VariablesAndBatches_Point3
data.value: Variables are kept internally in the temporary table __learnsql_variables. Do not use this name.

data.name: VariablesAndBatches_Point4
data.value: An assignment converts the value to the declared type. For VARCHAR(n) the text is truncated to n characters, and without a length the length is 1, as in MSSQL.

data.name: VariablesAndBatches_Point5
data.value: Variables of the same DECLARE statement cannot use each other. DECLARE @a INT = 1, @b INT = @a raises error 137 as in MSSQL, and only a separate DECLARE statement may read @a.

data.name: VariablesAndBatches_Point6
data.value: The output column of SELECT @x is named (No column name) as in MSSQL.

data.name: VariablesAndBatches_Point7
data.value: SELECT @x = ... is not available yet. Use SET @x = (SELECT ...).

data.name: VariablesAndBatches_Point8
data.value: Table variables and system variables such as @@ROWCOUNT are not available yet. @@IDENTITY and SCOPE_IDENTITY() return the most recently assigned ID.

data.name: SchemaObjects_Title
data.value: Tables, keys and temporary objects

data.name: SchemaObjects_Summary
data.value: The common DDL statements are translated. Some MSSQL properties have no equivalent in SQLite.

data.name: SchemaObjects_Point1
data.value: The schema dbo and INFORMATION_SCHEMA are omitted. There is only one schema, and other schema names are not available yet.

data.name: SchemaObjects_Point2
data.value: A column INT IDENTITY(1,1) PRIMARY KEY becomes INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT. Seed and increment are ignored, and the values start at 1.

data.name: SchemaObjects_Point3
data.value: SCOPE_IDENTITY() and @@IDENTITY return the most recently assigned ID. If nothing has been inserted yet, they return 0 instead of NULL.

data.name: SchemaObjects_Point4
data.value: Tables named #Name are temporary tables. SELECT ... INTO table becomes CREATE TABLE ... AS SELECT. TRUNCATE TABLE becomes DELETE FROM.

data.name: SchemaObjects_Point5
data.value: BEGIN TRAN, COMMIT, ROLLBACK and SAVE TRAN with savepoints are available. Nested transactions and @@TRANCOUNT do not exist.

data.name: SchemaObjects_Point6
data.value: CLUSTERED and NONCLUSTERED on indexes and keys are ignored. Table hints such as WITH (NOLOCK) and statements such as SET NOCOUNT ON are skipped.

data.name: SchemaObjects_Point7
data.value: ALTER TABLE supports adding one column and DROP COLUMN per statement. Create constraints in CREATE TABLE.

data.name: SchemaObjects_Point8
data.value: Foreign keys, UNIQUE, CHECK and NOT NULL are enforced as in MSSQL.

data.name: NotYetAvailable_Title
data.value: T-SQL constructs that are not available yet

data.name: NotYetAvailable_Summary
data.value: This environment recognizes these constructs but does not run them yet. They will be added step by step.
